title: Completing a register scan
statement: Let $P$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ deciders, let $D$ be a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes, and let $x$ be a Boolean input. Suppose node $l$ has call specification $cs$, the register selected by argument position $a$ is $rr$, and register $rr$ contains the buffer tape for a Boolean word $w$. If the machine starts in the scanning return phase for this register and its head positions $rp$ satisfy $rp(rr)+1=n$ for a natural number $n\le |w|$, then at time $n+1$ it has advanced to the return successor for argument position $a+1$, with register $rr$'s head at zero and all other register head positions unchanged. At every time $t\le n+1$, each register head either remains at its initial position or, for register $rr$, lies between $-1$ and the maximum of its initial position and $0$; the decider tape head positions remain unchanged throughout.
hypotheses_covered: $P,l_0,D,q_0$ are fixed; $x$ is a Boolean input
$w$ is a Boolean word; register $rr$ contains its buffer tape
$rt,dt,dp,out,ip$ are supplied register and decider tapes, decider head positions, output, and input-head position
For every natural $n$ and register head-position function $rp$, $rp(rr)+1=n$
